text:
rachel: installed redwoodctl via Homebrew on my M1 laptop and the binary path is wrong. `which redwoodctl` -> /opt/homebrew/bin/redwoodctl but when I run `redwoodctl version` it says 'config not found' and suggests running `redwoodctl login`.

tom: did brew symlink to /usr/local by any chance? M1 uses /opt/homebrew; older install scripts assume /usr/local and create a wrapper that points to the wrong cellar. What does `ls -l $(which redwoodctl)` show?

rachel: symlink points to /usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl/0.9.1/bin/redwoodctl (which doesn't exist). Homebrew upgrade must have moved it.

iker: separate but related: we recently added support for XDG config. If REDWOODCTL_HOME isn't set, we prefer XDG_CONFIG_HOME/redwoodctl over $HOME/.redwoodctl. Could be a path mismatch between the wrapper and the real binary. Also note some macOS installers set REDWOODCTL_HOME in /etc/profile which isn't loaded in non-login shells (VS Code terminal).

vicky: I hit a weird profile precedence bug: `redwoodctl local test --profile=staging` still reads tokens from $HOME/.redwoodctl/default if the mounted volume exists. Expected behavior: CLI flag > env > mounted. Repro:
```
export REDWOODCTL_HOME=$HOME/.redwoodctl_test
mkdir -p $HOME/.redwoodctl
# put a token in $HOME/.redwoodctl/default
redwoodctl local test --profile=staging --mount $HOME/.redwoodctl:/home/dev/.redwoodctl
# CLI inside container sees default token, not staging
```
Result: wrong profile used and tests fail.

rachel: whoa that matches what I'm seeing. The install wrapper probably sets REDWOODCTL_HOME implicitly to /usr/local/etc/redwoodctl which then points to the wrong dir and the mount masks it.

tom: actionable list: 1) Fix Homebrew formula to ensure cellar path updates atomically and wrapper uses `$(brew --prefix)/bin/redwoodctl` not hard-coded paths. 2) Make CLI respect explicit `--profile` even if mounted directory has defaults; check merge order in config loader. 3) Add a postinstall caveat to formula that warns about non-login shells on macOS and how to set REDWOODCTL_HOME.

iker: also propose: when mounting host dir into `local test`, if mount owner is root and the expected token file is not writable, we should detect that and either chown the directory to the container user UID or print a helpful error recommending `--mount-uid` option. We could default to creating a per-run temp volume if the host mount is readonly.

vicky: user-facing short-term workaround: `brew reinstall redwoodctl && brew link --overwrite redwoodctl` and run `export REDWOODCTL_HOME=$HOME/.redwoodctl_test` before spawning VS Code. For localtest: `docker run -v $HOME/.redwoodctl:/home/dev/.redwoodctl:rw --user $(id -u):$(id -g) ...` fixes perms.

deploy-bot: issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/homebrew-redwoodctl/issues/128 (labels: install, brew, macos)

rachel: tests/CI caught another flake: `cli.install_test` fails when Homebrew prefix is non-standard. Suggest adding matrix job where HOMEBREW_PREFIX=/opt/homebrew and /usr/local to avoid regressions.

tom: I'll take the formula fix + caveat PR. iker, can you own the config loader precedence change? vicky can own the localtest mount heuristics?

iker: yup will add unit tests for precedence and a small integration that simulates mounted dir owned by root.

vicky: will add a `--mount-uid` flag and a warning message when mount is not writable. Also doc patch for 'Running local test on macOS'.

rachel: thanks team. Marking resolved for now — re-open if brew reinstall doesn't fix it for M1 users. :rocket:
